MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 13, 2026
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Bucknum at 5:04 p.m., on January 13, 2026, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on January 8, 2026, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Ruesch
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

Staff Present:  Elaine Lister, City Manager
  Jerry Hill, Assistant City Manager
  John R. Harper, Interim City Attorney
  Ellis Chang, Director of Administrative Services

  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:05 pm Mayor Bucknum recessed to Closed Session. At the hour of 6:02 pm Mayor
Bucknum reconvened the meeting with four Council Members present with Mayor Pro Tem
Goodell absent.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Harper announced that staff analyzed three housing proposals regarding CS2 and
based upon that analysis, the city has selected one of those developers and staff has been directed
to commence negotiations and return to the Council with an agreement.

INVOCATION: Council Member Vasquez

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

  Sergeant Grant G. Gallatin.

 P2.  Presentation to Former Mayor Bob Ruesch

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Monique Goetz, M.V.: Thanked the Council for budgeting the cost of the welcome baskets for
the City’s Adopted Headquarters Battalion’s entry level marines.

City Council Minutes  2  January 13, 2026

her boldness on getting things down. He thanked former Mayor Ruesch for his past year as
Mayor with his patience and kindness.

Kieran Franich, M.V.: Spoke on the Community Character Trait of the Month Perseverance. He
gave examples of the trait perseverance.

Stacy Holmes, M.V.: Complained about the slurry sealing on his street with no handicap parking
signs made available.

Michael Schlesinger, M.V.: Spoke on the banning of small gas-powered mowers and leaf
blowers in Mission Viejo.

Jeff McBride, M.V.: Spoke out on dangerous conditions on intersection of Oso Parkway and
Felipe. He asked that the traffic pattern be changed.

Tom Moore, M.V.: Gave a shout-out to the new Coastline Pizza. Asked why the county
supervisors allowed the Orange County firefighting helicopter contract to lapse.

Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Spoke on Consent Calendar Item #17 request that we do as much as
possible for the intersection of La Paz and Marguerite to be more pedestrian friendly.

 CITY MANAGER REPORTS

City Manager Lister gave updates on a few business and development projects. She pointed out
that Wholesome Choice has been moving rather slowly, and that staff have had some public inquiry
and the City is ready to issue the tenant Improvement Plans, however the owner must first obtain
approvals from Orange County Health Department as well as Santa Margarita Water District. Staff
reached out to the business owner today and the city is going to try to facilitate some assistance
and will contact Orange County Health and the water district to see if we can speed things along
for everyone’s benefit. Next, City Manager Lister touched on the Shops at Mission Viejo
expansion project. The 50,000 square foot outdoor restaurant and retail are underway with the
utility and building pad work. The shell buildings should be completed during summer 2026 and
the businesses should be open before summer 2027, so there is a bit of delay between the shells
and the businesses occupancy. She stated that the Mission Hospital grading site and circulation is
on schedule with construction to commence this spring. The entire project will be phased in over
the next five to six years. She commented that the Costco gas station is underway, with
construction starting early spring and should be open to the public summer 2026. Lucid Car
Dealership will replace the former Infinity Dealership. The planning application has been
approved, and they have submitted plans for tenant improvements, exterior site work, and they
anticipate opening by fall of this year. Lastly, she announced that the city has a new medical office
building, with construction plans submitted at the end of 2025 and they are currently under review.

 CITY ATTORNEY REPORTS

No report given.

 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

 20.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

 Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley thanked the Mission Viejo Activities Committee for all their work hosting
and planning Santa’s arrival and Santa’s workshop. She also thanked city staff for the decorations
and lights throughout the city. Council Member Kelley also thanked the Marine Adoption
Committee for planning the Marine Christmas gift drive and Christmas party. She attended a
City Council Minutes  7  January 13, 2026
 ribbon cutting ceremony at Your Floor Company and Joy Bird furniture store. Council Member
Kelley announced that she attended the following events: Whoville Night Market, Mission Viejo
Animal Services volunteer holiday party, a presentation on human trafficking. She gave a shout
out to Monique Goetz for her work on the new marine baskets. Council Member Kelley highlighted
the Potoki Center for the Arts and stated how much the program has grown with revenue surpassing
the previous four fiscal years combined.

 Council Member Ruesch

 Council Member Ruesch commented that he had a great holiday with his daughter and family
 visiting from Spain. He addressed Mr. Moore’s public comments regarding the OCFA helicopter
 contract stating that this will be addressed this month by the board and to keep people at ease
 there is mutual aid always in place. He stated that he attended the 4th annual Hanukah celebration
 and had a great time with our Jewish community. Council Member Ruesch indicated that he is
 going to continue working on business development to continue to bring new business new life
 into our community. He announced that January 23 will be the first Jeronimo Tunnel Concert of
 the year. He reminded residents that this is a very popular event so plan to arrive early.

 Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez attended the Jane Austen Holiday Ball and said it was very well attended
and everyone had a great time. She also attended the Hanukah event. She highlighted her
daughter’s girl scout outing at Ivy Park and holiday baking with her daughters. She stated she is
excited the meeting is ending early so she can read The Secret Garden to her youngest daughter.

 Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum started off recapping the holiday mixer with the League of California Cities,
Orange County Business Council and Association of California Cities Orange County which was
held at the Orange County Museum of Art. She attended the holiday caroling at the Potocki Center.
Council Member Bucknum also encouraged residents to attend the upcoming Jeronimo Tunnel
Concert. She attended the Hanukah celebration and was very inspired by the Rabbi’s message. She
also attended the Whoville event as well as having the privilege for her husband and herself to be
Mr. and Mrs. Clause the last night of Santa’s Workshop. She gave a shout-out to Dirty Dog Pet
Wash where she took her dog for a bath. Mayor Bucknum asked for a monthly update from the
Police Chief and Fire Chief. She thanked the public commentors this evening and stated we will
look into some of the concerns mentioned.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:29 pm, with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, January 27, 2026, at 5:00 p.m.
